settings = read_global_settings()
print("settings folder :", scratch)
print("users before    :", [u.username for u in (settings.users or [])],
      [getattr(u, "role", "") for u in (settings.users or [])])
print("logins before   :", [login.username for login in (settings.user_logins or [])])
write_global_settings(settings)  # what a first boot leaves on disk

summary = bootstrap_admin_from_env()

settings = read_global_settings(refresh=True)
stored = {login.username: login.password for login in (settings.user_logins or [])}
print("logins after    :", sorted(stored))
value = stored.get(USERNAME, "")
print("plaintext kept  :", value == SECRET)
print("bcrypt hash     :", value.startswith("$2"))
print("roles after     :", [(u.username, getattr(u, "role", "")) for u in (settings.users or [])])

    user=CodxUserLogin(username=USERNAME, password=SECRET)

```py api/codx/junior/version.py
"""
Build provenance of the running API — what ``GET /api/health`` reports.

An unattended deployment is verified from *outside* the box: the provisioning
pipeline polls ``/api/health`` and has to assert that the build it asked for is
the build that answered. Without a version/ref in the payload the probe can only
assert "something returned HTML", which cannot tell a successful upgrade from a
stale container or from a rollback that never happened.

The values are baked into the image at build time (see
``codx-junior-installer/demo/Dockerfile`` and ``.github/workflows/release.yml``)
and can be overridden from the environment, so the same binary reports the same
thing under ``docker run -e ...``.

Every key is always present: the shape of the readiness probe is part of the
contract, documented in the installer's ``cloud/`` folder.
"""

import functools
import json
import os
import subprocess

BUILD_INFO_PATH = os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_INFO", "/etc/codx-junior/build-info.json")

# Directories probed for a checkout when the image carries no build descriptor
# (docker compose up on a clone, a dev run, a self-hosted install from source).
GIT_PATH_CANDIDATES = [
    path for path in (os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_PATH"), os.getcwd()) if path
]

GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 3

UNKNOWN = "unknown"


def _file_info() -> dict:
    """Read the build descriptor written at image build time (best effort)."""
    try:
        with open(BUILD_INFO_PATH, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            data = json.load(handle)
        return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def _git(*args: str, path: str) -> str:
    """Run one read-only git command, returning "" when it is not applicable."""
    try:
        result = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", path, *args],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
            check=False,
        )
    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
        return ""
    return result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def _git_info() -> dict:
    """Read the checkout the app runs from — the local / self-hosted case.

    An image built without the ``CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_*`` args has no descriptor,
    and reporting "unknown" forever makes the readiness probe useless. Reading
    the checkout keeps it honest. Cached: the probe is polled every few seconds
    and must not fork git on every request.
    """
    for path in GIT_PATH_CANDIDATES:
        commit = _git("rev-parse", "HEAD", path=path)
        if not commit:
            continue
        describe = _git("describe", "--tags", "--always", path=path)
        return {
            "version": describe or UNKNOWN,
            "ref": describe or UNKNOWN,
            "commit": commit,
        }
    return {}


def build_info() -> dict:
    """
    Return ``{"version", "ref", "commit"}`` — never raises, always complete.

    Precedence: environment > build descriptor baked into the image > the
    checkout the app runs from > "unknown". Environment wins so a deployment
    can report the ref it was installed from even when the image was built once
    for a whole release line.
    """
    info = _file_info()
    git = _git_info()

    def value(env_name: str, key: str) -> str:
        return str(os.environ.get(env_name) or info.get(key) or git.get(key) or UNKNOWN)

    return {
        "version": value("CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_VERSION", "version"),
        "ref": value("CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_REF", "ref"),
        "commit": value("CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_COMMIT", "commit"),
    }

```sh install.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# codx-junior — one-line installer / upgrader
#
# Root is required (it installs Docker); when it is not root it prints the exact
# command to run instead of escalating on its own.
#
#   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codx-junior/codx-junior/main/install.sh -o install.sh
#   sudo ./install.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxx
#
# It installs on a fresh machine and UPDATES an
# existing installation (the repository is moved to the requested branch, your
# projects and settings are kept).
#
# This file is deliberately small: it resolves the real installer of the
# requested branch (`codx-junior-installer/cloud/bootstrap.sh`) and hands the
# settings over to it, so there is exactly ONE place that knows how to install.
#
#   --branch, -branch, --ref, -b BRANCH   branch or tag to install/update (default: main)
#   --provider, -p NAME   AI provider preset: openai deepseek gemini
#                         openrouter mistral groq ollama custom.
#                         Default: keep the settings file value, else deepseek.
#   --key, -k KEY         provider API key (or --key-file)
#   --key-file PATH       read the key from a file
#   --url URL             OpenAI-compatible endpoint (only for provider `custom`)
#   --model ID            override the preset chat model
#   --port, -P PORT       web port                                default: 19981
#   --projects PATH       folder holding your projects            default: <home>/projects
#   --home PATH           installation root                       default: /opt/codx-junior
#   --repo URL            git repository to install from
#   --env-file PATH       settings file                       default: /etc/codx-junior/settings.env
#   --installer PATH      use this bootstrap.sh instead of the one of the branch
#   --build               build the image from source instead of pulling it
#   --domain DOMAIN       serve HTTPS on DOMAIN (automatic ACME, no extra tool)
#   --tls none            do not terminate TLS here: a proxy in front forwards
#                         to the web port
#   --non-interactive     never wait for input: fail instead of prompting
#                         (also CODX_JUNIOR_NON_INTERACTIVE=1)
#   --no-docker-install   fail instead of installing Docker
#   --open-firewall       ufw: allow ssh + the web port (off by default)
#   --update              update an existing installation (the default)
#   --dry-run             show what would run; change nothing
#   -h, --help            this help
#   -V, --version         print the version of this installer script
#
# Every value can also come from the environment (CODX_JUNIOR_REF,
# CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER, CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY, CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT, …) and
# from --env-file. Precedence: default < env file < environment < flags.
#
# Exit code 0 means codx-junior answered its health check.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

INSTALLER_VERSION="0.0.1"
DEFAULT_REPO="https://github.com/codx-junior/codx-junior.git"
DEFAULT_REF="main"

log()  { printf '\033[1;32m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
die()  { printf '\033[1;31mERROR:\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

usage() {
    # Printed from here (not from the file header) because when this script is
    # piped into bash, $BASH_SOURCE is empty and there is nothing to sed.
    cat <<'USAGE'
codx-junior installer — one line, installs or updates

  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codx-junior/codx-junior/main/install.sh \
    -o install.sh
  sudo ./install.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxx

  ./install.sh --provider openai --key sk-xxxxxxxx          # from a checkout
  ./install.sh --branch feature-x --provider gemini --key AIza...

Settings (flag | environment | --env-file), lowest precedence first:
  --branch, -branch, --ref, -b  BRANCH   branch or tag to install/update   [main]
  --provider, -p                NAME     openai deepseek gemini openrouter
                                         mistral groq ollama custom
                                         [settings file, else deepseek]
  --key, -k                     KEY      provider API key (or --key-file)
  --key-file                    PATH     read the key from a file
  --url                         URL      endpoint, only for provider `custom`
  --model                       ID       override the preset chat model
  --port, -P                    PORT     web port                       [19981]
  --projects                    PATH     folder for your projects  [<home>/projects]
  --home                        PATH     installation root          [/opt/codx-junior]
  --repo                        URL      git repository to install from
  --env-file                    PATH     settings file  [/etc/codx-junior/settings.env]
  --installer                   PATH     use this bootstrap.sh for the install
  --build                                build the image instead of pulling it
  --domain                     DOMAIN    serve HTTPS on DOMAIN (automatic ACME)
  --tls                        MODE      `none` = a proxy in front terminates
                                         TLS (default with --domain: caddy)
  --non-interactive, --yes, -y           never wait for input: fail instead
  --no-docker-install                    fail instead of installing Docker
  --open-firewall                        ufw: allow ssh + the web port
  --update                               update an existing install (default)
  --dry-run                              show what would run; change nothing
  -h, --help | -V, --version

Environment equivalent of every flag: CODX_JUNIOR_REF, CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER,
CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY, CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL, CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL,
CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT, CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH, CODX_JUNIOR_HOME,
CODX_JUNIOR_REPO, CODX_JUNIOR_ENV_FILE, CODX_JUNIOR_INSTALLER,
CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD, CODX_JUNIOR_INSTALL_DOCKER, CODX_JUNIOR_OPEN_FIREWALL,
CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN, CODX_JUNIOR_TLS, CODX_JUNIOR_NON_INTERACTIVE,
CODX_JUNIOR_PUBLIC_URL, CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_USER, CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_PASSWORD.

From a checkout: ./install.sh …   As root, or with sudo in front of it.
USAGE
}

need() {
    [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "${2:-}" ]] || die "option $1 needs a value (see --help)"
}

# --- settings: environment first, flags afterwards --------------------------
REF="${CODX_JUNIOR_REF:-${DEFAULT_REF}}"
REPO="${CODX_JUNIOR_REPO:-${DEFAULT_REPO}}"
PROVIDER="${CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER:-}"
API_KEY="${CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY:-}"
API_KEY_FILE="${CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY_FILE:-}"
API_URL="${CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL:-}"
MODEL="${CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL:-}"
PORT="${CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT:-}"
PROJECTS="${CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH:-}"
HOME_DIR="${CODX_JUNIOR_HOME:-}"
ENV_FILE="${CODX_JUNIOR_ENV_FILE:-}"
INSTALLER="${CODX_JUNIOR_INSTALLER:-}"
BUILD="${CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD:-0}"
INSTALL_DOCKER="${CODX_JUNIOR_INSTALL_DOCKER:-1}"
OPEN_FIREWALL="${CODX_JUNIOR_OPEN_FIREWALL:-0}"
DOMAIN="${CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN:-}"
TLS_MODE="${CODX_JUNIOR_TLS:-}"
NON_INTERACTIVE="${CODX_JUNIOR_NON_INTERACTIVE:-0}"
DRY_RUN=0
UPDATE_ONLY=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --branch|--ref|-branch|-ref|-b|-r)  need "$@"; REF="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --provider|-provider|-p)            need "$@"; PROVIDER="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --key|-key|-k)                      need "$@"; API_KEY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --key-file|-key-file)               need "$@"; API_KEY_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --url|-url|-u)                      need "$@"; API_URL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --model|-model|-m)                  need "$@"; MODEL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --port|-port|-P)                    need "$@"; PORT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --projects|-projects)               need "$@"; PROJECTS="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --home|-home)                       need "$@"; HOME_DIR="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --repo|-repo)                       need "$@"; REPO="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --env-file|-env-file)               need "$@"; ENV_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --installer|-installer)             need "$@"; INSTALLER="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --build|-build)                     BUILD=1; shift ;;
        --no-docker-install)                INSTALL_DOCKER=0; shift ;;
        --open-firewall)                    OPEN_FIREWALL=1; shift ;;
        --domain)                           need "$@"; DOMAIN="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --tls)                              need "$@"; TLS_MODE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --non-interactive|--yes|-y)         NON_INTERACTIVE=1; shift ;;
        --update|-update)                   UPDATE_ONLY=1; shift ;;
        --dry-run|--dry|--check)            DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help|-help)                    usage; exit 0 ;;
        -V|--version|-version)              printf 'codx-junior install.sh %s\n' "${INSTALLER_VERSION}"; exit 0 ;;
        "")                                 shift ;;
        *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    esac
done

# The branch lands in a URL and in a git ref: keep it boring on purpose.
[[ "${REF}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$ ]] || die "invalid branch name: ${REF}"
[[ "${PORT}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ || -z "${PORT}" ]] || die "invalid port: ${PORT}"
[[ -z "${DOMAIN}" || "${DOMAIN}" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+$ ]] || die "invalid domain: ${DOMAIN}"
[[ -z "${TLS_MODE}" || "${TLS_MODE}" == "none" ]] \
    || die "invalid --tls value: ${TLS_MODE} (only 'none' is supported)"

if [[ -z "${API_KEY}" && -n "${API_KEY_FILE}" ]]; then
    [[ -f "${API_KEY_FILE}" ]] || die "key file not found: ${API_KEY_FILE}"
    # `read` stops at the newline and needs no command substitution, so the
    # value never reaches the process list.
    IFS= read -r API_KEY < "${API_KEY_FILE}" || true
    API_KEY=${API_KEY%%$'\r'}
fi

# --- resolve the real installer for the requested branch --------------------
REAL_INSTALLER=""
RESOLVED_HOW=""

LOCAL_INSTALLER=""
if [[ -n "${INSTALLER}" ]]; then
    LOCAL_INSTALLER="${INSTALLER}"
elif [[ -n "${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-}" && -f "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" ]]; then
    # Running from a file: prefer the checkout this script belongs to.
    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    if [[ -f "${SCRIPT_DIR}/codx-junior-installer/cloud/bootstrap.sh" ]]; then
        LOCAL_INSTALLER="${SCRIPT_DIR}/codx-junior-installer/cloud/bootstrap.sh"
    fi
fi

if [[ -n "${LOCAL_INSTALLER}" ]]; then
    [[ -f "${LOCAL_INSTALLER}" ]] || die "installer not found: ${LOCAL_INSTALLER}"
    REAL_INSTALLER="${LOCAL_INSTALLER}"
    RESOLVED_HOW="local"
fi

# raw.githubusercontent needs no git and no clone, which matters on a bare VM.
raw_url() {
    local url="${REPO%.git}" owner repo
    url="${url#git@github.com:}"
    url="${url#ssh://git@github.com/}"
    url="${url#https://github.com/}"
    [[ "${url}" == */* ]] || return 1
    owner="${url%%/*}"
    repo="${url#*/}"
    [[ "${REPO}" == *github.com* ]] || return 1
    printf 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/%s/%s/%s/codx-junior-installer/cloud/bootstrap.sh' \
        "${owner}" "${repo}" "${REF}"
}

TMP_INSTALLER=""
cleanup() {
    [[ -n "${TMP_INSTALLER}" && -f "${TMP_INSTALLER}" ]] && rm -f "${TMP_INSTALLER}" || true
}
trap cleanup EXIT

if [[ -z "${REAL_INSTALLER}" ]]; then
    TMP_INSTALLER="$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/codx-junior-bootstrap.XXXXXX.sh")"
    URL="$(raw_url || true)"
    FETCHED=0
    if [[ -n "${URL}" ]]; then
        if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            curl -fsSL --max-time 60 "${URL}" -o "${TMP_INSTALLER}" 2>/dev/null && FETCHED=1
        elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            wget -qO "${TMP_INSTALLER}" "${URL}" 2>/dev/null && FETCHED=1
        fi
        if [[ "${FETCHED}" == "1" ]]; then
            RESOLVED_HOW="downloaded (${REF})"
        fi
    fi

    if [[ "${FETCHED}" != "1" ]]; then
        # Unknown host or no raw endpoint: get the branch with git instead.
        command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || die "cannot download the installer and git is not installed (see --installer)"
        CLONE_DIR="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/codx-junior-src.XXXXXX")"
        log "Fetching the installer with git (${REPO} @ ${REF})"
        git clone --depth 1 --branch "${REF}" "${REPO}" "${CLONE_DIR}" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
            || die "cannot clone ${REPO} at ${REF} (does the branch exist?)"
        REAL_INSTALLER="${CLONE_DIR}/codx-junior-installer/cloud/bootstrap.sh"
        [[ -f "${REAL_INSTALLER}" ]] \
            || die "unexpected repository layout: ${REAL_INSTALLER} is missing"
        RESOLVED_HOW="cloned (${REF})"
    else
        REAL_INSTALLER="${TMP_INSTALLER}"
    fi
fi

# --- forward everything explicitly (flags survive sudo, env vars do not) ----
FORWARD=(--ref "${REF}")

```md codx-junior-installer/cloud/DEPLOYMENT-CONTRACT.md
# codx-junior — unattended deployment contract

Everything below is the *supported* way to install codx-junior on a machine nobody
touches: a cloud VM bootstrapped by cloud-init, a hosted workspace, a CI runner.
If a step here is not honoured by the code, that is a bug in this repository, not
a gap in your automation.

Status of each item is stated explicitly. `[verified]` = exercised by the code in
this tree; `[unverified]` = implemented but never run on a real VM from here.

```
settings file ──▶ install.sh ──▶ codx-junior-installer/cloud/bootstrap.sh ──▶ docker compose
   (root 0600)     (one entry         (host prep, clone, domain/TLS)          (pull only)
                     point)
```

---

## 1. The settings file

`/etc/codx-junior/settings.env`, root:root, mode `0600`, passed with
`--env-file`. Precedence, lowest first: **default < settings file < environment < flag**.

| key | honoured | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` | `[verified]` | `openai` `deepseek` `gemini` `openrouter` `ollama` `custom` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` | `[verified]` | provider key; omitted for `ollama` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` | `[verified]` | override the preset model |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` | `[verified]` | OpenAI-compatible endpoint (required for `custom`) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT` | `[verified]` | published port, default `19981` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_REF` | `[verified]` | branch **or tag** to install/update; default `main` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` | `[verified]` | data folder, keep it outside the clone; default `./projects` |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PUBLIC_URL` | `[verified]` | the URL the instance believes it is served on (links, OAuth redirects, websockets) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_DOMAIN` | `[verified]` | enables the bundled TLS front door (see §4) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_NON_INTERACTIVE` | `[verified]` | `1` = never prompt (see §3) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_USER` | `[verified]` | first admin username (see §5) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | `[verified]` | first admin password, bcrypt-hashed, never logged |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_EMAIL` | `[verified]` | first admin email (optional) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE` | `[verified]` | force the container image; overrides the ref→tag mapping |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_*` | `[verified]` | `VERSION`/`REF`/`COMMIT` reported by `/api/health`; set by the release build, not by you |

`CODX_JUNIOR_REF`, `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` and `CODX_JUNIOR_PUBLIC_URL` are
confirmed: keep writing them exactly as you do today.

**Upgrades never touch data.** `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` lives outside the
checkout, so re-running the installer upgrades code and leaves every project,
chat and database file untouched.

---

## 2. Install paths, minimum box, wall clock

| path | how | minimum box | wall clock | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **pull** (supported for unattended installs) | `install.sh --ref <tag>` | 2 vCPU / 4 GB / 40 GB | ~3-6 min (image pull dominates) | nothing is compiled on the box |
| **build** (developers, explicit) | `install.sh ... ` then `demo/up.sh --build` | 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 20 GB free | ~20 min | `--build` is the *only* way to compile |

A failed pull is **fatal** (`[verified]`, `demo/up.sh`): the installer prints the
tag, the `--build` alternative and "nothing was started", then exits non-zero.
There is no silent fallback to a build — on a paid 2 vCPU box that fallback used
to be a 20 minute compile with nobody watching.

### Pinning

```bash
install.sh --ref v1.2.3 --non-interactive </dev/null
```

* `vX.Y.Z` → image `codxjunior/codx-junior:vX.Y.Z` (`[verified]`)
* anything else (`main`, a branch name, a raw commit) → `codxjunior/codx-junior:demo`
* `--dev` (developers only) → `codxjunior/codx-junior:dev`, built from the checkout

The project is **pre-1.0**: the first release tag is `v0.0.1` and the installer
reports `install.sh 0.0.1`. Tags stay orderable (`v0.0.1` < `v0.1.0` < `v1.0.0`),
so pinning works exactly the same from the first one on — do not expect a `v1.x`
line before the API is frozen.

A release tag publishes its own image from `.github/workflows/release.yml`, so a
pinned ref is reproducible and rollbackable. **Do not track `main` in customer
infrastructure**: it is a moving branch and a broken commit breaks every new
workspace at once.

> Creating the tag itself is the repository owner's step (`git tag -a v1.2.3 -m ...`,
> `git push origin v1.2.3`). The workflow cannot tag on your behalf.

---

## 3. Non-interactive mode

```bash
sudo ./install.sh --env-file /etc/codx-junior/settings.env \
     --domain <slug>.example.com --non-interactive </dev/null
```

`--non-interactive`, `--yes`, `-y` or `CODX_JUNIOR_NON_INTERACTIVE=1`
(`[verified]`) guarantee:

* stdin is closed for the whole run, so a prompt becomes an **EOF failure**, never a hang;
* `DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive`, `NEEDRESTART_MODE=a` — apt never stops for a TTY;
* `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` — a private or misspelled repo fails instead of asking for credentials.

A missing required setting is a non-zero exit with the name of the setting, not a
default silently chosen for you.

---

## 4. HTTPS

Two supported modes, pick one:

```bash
# A) the installer owns TLS (Caddy, automatic ACME, ports 80+443)
./install.sh --domain x.example.com --non-interactive

# B) you already have a TLS terminator (Cloudflare, ALB, another proxy)
./install.sh --tls=none --non-interactive
```

Mode **A** (`[verified]` in `cloud/bootstrap.sh`): Caddy is started with
`80/443 → 127.0.0.1:<port>`, waits up to 3 minutes for a *valid* certificate
(verified with `--resolve x.example.com:443:127.0.0.1`), and fails loudly with the
DNS/ACME cause if it never appears. Requirements:

* the `A` record must already answer with this machine's IP — **publish DNS before
  the install**, otherwise the first ACME order burns the Let's Encrypt rate limit;
* `proxied = false` on Cloudflare, or ACME challenges never reach the box;
* ports 80 and 443 open (ufw is opened automatically when a domain is used).

Mode **B** forwards plain HTTP from your terminator; no certificate is requested.

---

## 5. First admin

An unattended install has nobody to fill a setup form, so the admin comes from the
settings file (`[verified]`, `api/codx/junior/security/admin_bootstrap.py`, run on
startup):

```env
CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_USER=admin
CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<generated per workspace>
CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.com
```

* bcrypt-hashed before storage; the plain password is never logged, never written
  to `db.json`, never echoed by the installer;
* it runs **once**: if any admin already exists the keys are ignored, so changing
  the password later is done from the UI and a stale `settings.env` cannot reset it;
* remove the key from the file after the first successful boot if your platform can
  rewrite it.

---

## 6. Readiness: `GET /api/health`

Unauthenticated, stable shape, always present keys — this is the probe to poll
instead of `/`:

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "version": "1.2.3",
  "ref": "v1.2.3",
  "commit": "9f1ab2c3d4e5",
  "uptime_seconds": 41.7,
  "event_loop_lag_ms": { "last_ms": 1.2, "max_ms": 18.0 },
  "projects_cached": 1,
  "api_log_pipeline": { "queue_depth": 0, "written_events": 12 }
}
```

`version` / `ref` / `commit` come from the image build (`[verified]`,
`api/codx/junior/version.py`); they answer `"unknown"` only for a local
`--build`, which is exactly what you want to detect.

Polling recipe (what the shipped `cloud/bootstrap.sh` does):

```bash
until curl -fsS "https://x.example.com/api/health" > /tmp/health.json; do sleep 5; done
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
h = json.load(open("/tmp/health.json"))
assert h["status"] == "ok"
assert h["ref"] == "v1.2.3", h          # the ref we asked for, not "something"
PY
```

---

## 7. What a successful install guarantees

1. the image was **pulled**, not compiled (`--build` absent);
2. the published port answers `GET /api/health` with `status=ok`;
3. `ref`/`commit` match the ref that was requested;
4. when `--domain` is used, `https://<domain>/api/health` answers with a valid certificate;
5. when the admin keys are set, `POST /api/users/login` accepts them.

Anything else is a failed install: the installer exits non-zero and starts nothing
(§2) or fails at the step that broke (§4).

---

## 8. Known gaps

* The release workflow has never run in this repository (no tag exists yet), so
  the first `v*` push is its real smoke test. Until then a pinned `--ref vX.Y.Z`
  fails at the pull — loudly, by design.
* `demo/up.sh --build` reports `"unknown"` build provenance; `--dev` and release
  images both carry a real `version`/`ref`/`commit` (from `git describe` and
  from the CI build args respectively).
* `.codx` is the control plane. `.dockerignore` drops only the **generated** data
  plane (chat turns, browser sessions, atlas, db, logs — 1.5 GB on a developer
  box) and keeps every tracked artifact (profiles, tasks, boards, views, teams,
  workspaces) in the context, so `./up.sh --dev` builds against the real control
  plane. The release image never `COPY`s `.codx`: it is created at first boot
  inside the `codx-junior-settings` volume. **Nothing is untracked from the
  repository** — no `git rm --cached`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# codx-junior demo — one command to a working instance
#
#   ./up.sh                                  # reads .env (created from .env.example)
#   ./up.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-...  # configures .env for you
#   ./up.sh --build                           # build the image locally (developers)
#
# What it does: validate the settings you must pass, pull the image, start the
# stack, wait until the API reports healthy and apply the AI provider
# configuration. Idempotent: running it again just restarts the stack.
#
# Knowledge / RAG is built in (embedded LanceDB): there is no extra service to
# start, only an embeddings provider, which the preset already configures.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}"

ENV_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/.env"
EXAMPLE_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/.env.example"
CONTAINER="codx-junior-demo"

PROVIDER=""
API_KEY=""
PORT=""
PROJECTS=""
DO_BUILD=0
DO_DEV=0
NON_INTERACTIVE=0

usage() {
    cat <<USAGE
codx-junior demo installer

Usage: ./up.sh [options]

  --provider <name>   which provider preset to use; it also defines the models
                      (openai | deepseek | gemini | openrouter | mistral | groq | ollama | custom)
  --key <api-key>     API key of the provider (also read from CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY)
  --list-providers    Show every provider preset with the models it configures, then exit
  --url <base-url>    OpenAI-compatible endpoint (required for `custom`)
  --model <model-id>  Override the default chat model of the provider
  --port <port>       Web port (default 19981)
  --projects <path>   Host folder that holds your projects (default ./projects)
  --build             Build the image from source instead of pulling it
  --dev               Developer flavour: build from this checkout as
                      `codxjunior/codx-junior:dev`, with the whole repository
                      (control plane included) mounted on top of the image, so
                      nothing has to be baked in. Implies --build.
  --no-wait           Do not wait for the health check
  --non-interactive   Promise that no prompt will ever appear. up.sh never
                      prompts today; the flag exists so an unattended caller
                      (install.sh, cloud/bootstrap.sh) can pass it uniformly
  -h, --help          This help
USAGE
}

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --provider) PROVIDER="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --key)      API_KEY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --url)      CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --model)    MODEL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --port)     PORT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --projects) PROJECTS="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --build)    DO_BUILD=1; shift ;;
        --dev)      DO_DEV=1; DO_BUILD=1; shift ;;
        --no-wait)  NO_WAIT=1; shift ;;
        --non-interactive|--yes|-y) NON_INTERACTIVE=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help)  usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; usage; exit 1 ;;
    esac
done

# --- settings may also come from the environment ---------------------------
# Precedence: command line flag > environment > .env. The environment path is
# what lets an automated deployment (cloud-init, Ansible, CI) configure the
# instance without passing flags:
#   CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER=deepseek CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY=sk-... ./up.sh

API_KEY="${API_KEY:-${CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY:-}}"

NO_WAIT="${NO_WAIT:-0}"

log()  { printf '\033[1;32m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
die()  { printf '\033[1;31mERROR:\033[0m %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

# --- docker ----------------------------------------------------------------
command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "Docker is not installed (https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)."
docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "The Docker daemon is not running."
if docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    COMPOSE=(docker compose)
elif command -v docker-compose >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    COMPOSE=(docker-compose)
else
    die "docker compose (v2) is required."
fi

# --- .env helpers ----------------------------------------------------------
set_env_var() {
    # Replace the first (possibly commented) KEY=... line, else append.
    local key="$1" value="$2" file="$3"
    if grep -Eq "^#?[[:space:]]*${key}=" "$file"; then
        awk -v k="$key" -v v="$value" '
            $0 ~ "^#?[[:space:]]*" k "=" && !done { print k "=" v; done=1; next }

        printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$value" >> "$file"
    fi

  ./up.sh --provider openai   --key sk-xxxxxxxx
  ./up.sh --provider gemini   --key AIza-xxxxxxxx

Supported: openai, deepseek, gemini, openrouter, mistral, groq, ollama, custom.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# codx-junior demo — one command to a working instance
#
#   ./up.sh                                  # reads .env (created from .env.example)
#   ./up.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-...  # configures .env for you

# What it does: validate the settings you must pass, pull the image, start the
# stack, wait until the API reports healthy and apply the AI provider
# configuration. Idempotent: running it again just restarts the stack.
#
# Knowledge / RAG is built in (embedded LanceDB): there is no extra service to
# start, only an embeddings provider, which the preset already configures.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}"

ENV_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/.env"
EXAMPLE_FILE="${SCRIPT_DIR}/.env.example"
CONTAINER="codx-junior-demo"

PROVIDER=""
API_KEY=""
PORT=""
PROJECTS=""
DO_BUILD=0
DO_DEV=0
NON_INTERACTIVE=0

usage() {
    cat <<USAGE
codx-junior demo installer

Usage: ./up.sh [options]

  --provider <name>   which provider preset to use; it also defines the models
                      (openai | deepseek | gemini | openrouter | mistral | groq | ollama | custom)
  --key <api-key>     API key of the provider (also read from CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY)
  --list-providers    Show every provider preset with the models it configures, then exit
  --url <base-url>    OpenAI-compatible endpoint (required for custom)
  --model <model-id>  Override the default chat model of the provider
  --port <port>       Web port (default 19981)
  --projects <path>   Host folder that holds your projects (default ./projects)
  --build             Build the image from source instead of pulling it
  --dev               Developer flavour: build from this checkout as
                      codxjunior/codx-junior:dev, with the whole repository
                      (control plane included) mounted on top of the image, so
                      nothing has to be baked in. Implies --build.
  --no-wait           Do not wait for the health check
  --non-interactive   Promise that no prompt will ever appear. up.sh never
                      prompts today; the flag exists so an unattended caller
                      (install.sh, cloud/bootstrap.sh) can pass it uniformly
  -h, --help          This help
USAGE
}

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --provider) PROVIDER="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --key)      API_KEY="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --url)      CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --model)    MODEL="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --port)     PORT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --projects) PROJECTS="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
        --build)    DO_BUILD=1; shift ;;
        --dev)      DO_DEV=1; DO_BUILD=1; shift ;;
        --no-wait)  NO_WAIT=1; shift ;;
        --non-interactive|--yes|-y) NON_INTERACTIVE=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help)  usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; usage; exit 1 ;;
    esac

# Precedence: command line flag > environment > .env. The environment path is
# what lets an automated deployment (cloud-init, Ansible, CI) configure the
# instance without passing flags:

NO_WAIT="${NO_WAIT:-0}"

log()  { printf '\033[1;32m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf '\033[1;33m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }

elif command -v docker-compose >/dev/null 2>&1; then

set_env_var() {

            $0 ~ "^#?[[:space:]]*" k "=" && !done { print k "=" v; done=1; next }
            { print }
        ' "$file" > "${file}.tmp"
        mv "${file}.tmp" "$file"
    else
        printf '%s=%s\n' "$key" "$value" >> "$file"
    fi
}

get_env_var() {
    local key="$1" file="$2"
    [ -f "$file" ] || return 0
    grep -E "^${key}=" "$file" | tail -n1 | cut -d= -f2- || true
}

[ -f "${ENV_FILE}" ] || { cp "${EXAMPLE_FILE}" "${ENV_FILE}"; log "Created .env from .env.example"; }

[[ -n "${PROVIDER}" ]] && set_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER "${PROVIDER}" "${ENV_FILE}"
[[ -n "${API_KEY}"  ]] && set_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY  "${API_KEY}"  "${ENV_FILE}"
[[ -n "${CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL:-}" ]] && set_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL "${CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL}" "${ENV_FILE}"
[[ -n "${MODEL}"    ]] && set_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL    "${MODEL}"    "${ENV_FILE}"
[[ -n "${PORT}"     ]] && set_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT    "${PORT}"     "${ENV_FILE}"
[[ -n "${PROJECTS}" ]] && set_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH "${PROJECTS}" "${ENV_FILE}"
# First admin account. An unattended install has nobody to fill the "create the
# first user" form, so the credentials travel with the settings and the API
# stores them as a bcrypt hash on first boot (see
# api/codx/junior/security/admin_bootstrap.py). .env is chmod 600 above and the
# values are never printed.
[[ -n "${CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_USER:-}" ]]     && set_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_USER     "${CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_USER}"     "${ENV_FILE}"
[[ -n "${CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-}" ]] && set_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_PASSWORD "${CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_PASSWORD}" "${ENV_FILE}"
[[ -n "${CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_EMAIL:-}" ]]    && set_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_EMAIL    "${CODX_JUNIOR_ADMIN_EMAIL}"    "${ENV_FILE}"

FINAL_PROVIDER="$(get_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER "${ENV_FILE}")"
FINAL_KEY="$(get_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY "${ENV_FILE}")"
FINAL_URL="$(get_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL "${ENV_FILE}")"
WEB_PORT="$(get_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT "${ENV_FILE}")"
WEB_PORT="${WEB_PORT:-19981}"
PROJECTS_PATH="$(get_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH "${ENV_FILE}")"
PROJECTS_PATH="${PROJECTS_PATH:-./projects}"
# Printed in the summary. On a cloud VM localhost is not what the user opens,
# so a deployment script can pass the address it published (see cloud/).
CODX_JUNIOR_PUBLIC_URL="${CODX_JUNIOR_PUBLIC_URL:-}"
if [[ -n "${CODX_JUNIOR_PUBLIC_URL}" ]]; then
    WEB_URL="${CODX_JUNIOR_PUBLIC_URL}"
else
    WEB_URL="http://localhost:${WEB_PORT}"
fi

if [[ -z "${FINAL_PROVIDER}" || -z "${FINAL_KEY}" ]]; then
    cat >&2 <<MISSING
ERROR: codx-junior needs an AI provider before it can do anything.

  ./up.sh --provider deepseek --key sk-xxxxxxxx
  ./up.sh --provider openai   --key sk-xxxxxxxx
  ./up.sh --provider gemini   --key AIza-xxxxxxxx

Supported: openai, deepseek, gemini, openrouter, mistral, groq, ollama, custom.
`custom` also needs --url https://your-gateway/v1
Alternatively edit ${ENV_FILE} (see README.md).
MISSING
    exit 1
fi

if [[ "${FINAL_PROVIDER}" == "custom" && -z "${FINAL_URL}" ]]; then
    die "provider 'custom' needs --url (an OpenAI-compatible endpoint ending in /v1)."
fi

# Project folder must exist and be absolute for the bind mount.
mkdir -p "${PROJECTS_PATH}"
PROJECTS_PATH="$(cd "${PROJECTS_PATH}" && pwd)"
set_env_var CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH "${PROJECTS_PATH}" "${ENV_FILE}"
log "Projects folder: ${PROJECTS_PATH}"

# --- image tag -------------------------------------------------------------
# `--dev` is the only flavour that runs the checkout instead of a release
# artifact: it builds locally and tags `:dev`, and the overlay compose file
# mounts the repository (control plane included) on top of the container.
# Release tags (vX.Y.Z...) pull their own image; anything else keeps the rolling
# tag. A pull-only install never reads the checkout, so tracking `:demo` while
# asking for `v1.2.3` would silently run whatever was published last.
if [[ "${DO_DEV}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE="codxjunior/codx-junior:dev"
    # Build provenance for a local build: `git describe` gives `v0.0.1`, which
    # is what `/api/health` then reports (release images get it from CI).
    repo_dir="${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.."
    if [[ -z "${CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_VERSION:-}" ]]; then
        CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_VERSION="$(git -C "${repo_dir}" describe --tags --always 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
    fi
    CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_COMMIT="${CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_COMMIT:-$(git -C "${repo_dir}" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)}"
    export CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_VERSION CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_COMMIT
elif [[ -z "${CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE:-}" ]]; then
    IMAGE_REF="${CODX_JUNIOR_REF:-}"
    if [[ "${IMAGE_REF}" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+ ]]; then
        CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE="codxjunior/codx-junior:${IMAGE_REF}"
    else
        CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE="codxjunior/codx-junior:demo"
    fi
fi
export CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE

# --- start -----------------------------------------------------------------
COMPOSE_FILES=(-f docker-compose.yaml)
[[ "${DO_DEV}" -eq 1 ]] && COMPOSE_FILES+=(-f docker-compose.dev.yaml)
COMPOSE_PROFILES=()

if [[ "${DO_BUILD}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    log "Building the demo image (first build takes a few minutes)..."
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" "${COMPOSE_FILES[@]}" "${COMPOSE_PROFILES[@]}" build
else
    log "Pulling ${CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE}..."
    if ! "${COMPOSE[@]}" "${COMPOSE_FILES[@]}" pull --quiet codx-junior; then
        # NEVER fall back to a build here. An unattended install (cloud-init)
        # has nobody to notice that "1-2 min pull" became a 20+ min compile on a
        # 2 vCPU box: it just burns a paid machine until the pipeline times out.
        # `--build` is the explicit opt-in for compiling and says so in --help.
        die "Could not pull ${CODX_JUNIOR_IMAGE}.
       Check the tag and the network access of this host, or install from
       source with --build (>= 4 vCPU / 8 GB / 20 GB free, ~20 min).
       Nothing was started, so it is safe to re-run."
    fi
fi

log "Starting codx-junior..."
"${COMPOSE[@]}" "${COMPOSE_FILES[@]}" "${COMPOSE_PROFILES[@]}" up -d --remove-orphans

if [[ "${NO_WAIT}" -ne 1 ]]; then
    log "Waiting for the API to become healthy (first start ~30s)..."
    STATUS="starting"
    for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
        STATUS="$(docker inspect -f '{{if .State.Health}}{{.State.Health.Status}}{{else}}running{{end}}' "${CONTAINER}" 2>/dev/null || echo starting)"
        [[ "${STATUS}" == "healthy" ]] && break
        if [[ "${STATUS}" == "unhealthy" || "${STATUS}" == "exited" ]]; then
            echo
            "${COMPOSE[@]}" "${COMPOSE_FILES[@]}" logs --tail 60 codx-junior || true
            die "codx-junior did not start (${STATUS}). Logs above."
        fi
        sleep 2
    done
    [[ "${STATUS}" == "healthy" ]] || { "${COMPOSE[@]}" "${COMPOSE_FILES[@]}" logs --tail 60 codx-junior || true; die "Health check timeout."; }
fi

# --- AI provider configuration --------------------------------------------
log "Configuring the AI provider from the environment..."
docker exec "${CONTAINER}" \
    curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap/apply >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || warn "Could not apply the provider automatically; check the container logs."

SUMMARY="$(docker exec "${CONTAINER}" curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -n "${SUMMARY}" ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' "${SUMMARY}"
fi

cat <<DONE

=============================================================================
 codx-junior is running

   Web UI : ${WEB_URL}
   Projects: ${PROJECTS_PATH}
   Settings: ${ENV_FILE}

 Next steps
   1. Open the UI and pick (or create) a project.
   2. Ask something in the chat - the provider is already configured.

 Logs / stop
   ${COMPOSE[*]} -f docker-compose.yaml logs -f codx-junior
   ${COMPOSE[*]} -f docker-compose.yaml down
=============================================================================
DONE

```

### Developer flavour: `./up.sh --dev`

Developers want the *real* control plane of the checkout they are working on —
tasks, boards, profiles, chat turns — and they want it live, without rebuilding
the image every time one of those files changes. `--dev` does exactly that:

```bash
./up.sh --dev        # builds codxjunior/codx-junior:dev from this checkout
```

* it builds the image locally (`:dev`) instead of pulling a release artifact;
* it adds `docker-compose.dev.yaml`, which mounts the **whole `<repo>/.codx`**

control plane stays in git, and only the *generated* data plane
(`.codx/db`, `.codx/atlas`, chat turns, browser sessions, logs…) is ignored by
git and kept out of the **release** image build context — it is runtime state,
it is large, and the release image recreates it at first boot inside the
`codx-junior-settings` volume. `--dev` gets all of it anyway, through the mount.

# =============================================================================
# codx-junior — DEV overlay (used by `./up.sh --dev`, never by an install)
#
# The release image carries no control plane on purpose: `.codx` is state, it is
# created at first boot and it persists in the `codx-junior-settings` volume.
# A developer, on the other hand, wants the real thing — tasks, boards, profiles
# and chat turns of the checkout he is working on — without baking 1.5 GB of
# runtime data into an image and without rebuilding every time it changes.
#
# So the `-dev` flavour mounts the repository instead of copying it:
#   * build from this checkout            -> `codxjunior/codx-junior:dev`
#   * <repo>/.codx -> the app's `.codx`   -> live control plane, read/write
#
# `up.sh --dev` sets CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_* from `git describe`, so the dev image
# reports a real `version`/`ref`/`commit` on /api/health too.
# =============================================================================
services:
  codx-junior:
    build:
      context: ../..
      dockerfile: codx-junior-installer/demo/Dockerfile
      args:
        CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_VERSION: ${CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_VERSION:-unknown}
        CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_REF: ${CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_VERSION:-unknown}
        CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_COMMIT: ${CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_COMMIT:-unknown}
    volumes:
      # The control plane of this checkout, live. Anything the container writes
      # (chat turns, boards, profiles) lands in the repository: that is the
      # point of the dev flavour, and it is also why the release image does not
      # do this.
      - ../../.codx:/home/codx-junior/codx-junior/.codx

### Developer flavour: `./up.sh --dev`

A developer wants the *real* control plane of the checkout being worked on
(tasks, boards, profiles, chat turns) and wants it live, without rebuilding the
image each time one of those files changes. `--dev` does exactly that:

```bash
./up.sh --dev        # builds codxjunior/codx-junior:dev from this checkout
```

* it builds the image locally (`:dev`) instead of pulling a release artifact;
* it adds `docker-compose.dev.yaml`, which mounts the **whole `<repo>/.codx`**
  over the container's control plane, read/write;
* `up.sh` fills `CODX_JUNIOR_BUILD_*` from `git describe`, so the dev image also
  reports a real `version`/`ref`/`commit` on `/api/health`.

control plane stays in git. Only the *generated* data plane (`.codx/db`,
`.codx/atlas`, `.codx/chat_turns`, browser sessions, logs…) is ignored by git and
kept out of the **release** image build context: it is runtime state, it is
large, and the release image recreates it at first boot inside the
`codx-junior-settings` volume. `--dev` still sees all of it, through the mount.

| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` | **yes** | `sk-…` | Key of that provider |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` | only for `custom` | `https://gw.acme.com/v1` | Override the preset endpoint |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` | no | `deepseek-chat` | Override the preset chat model |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH` | no | `~/my-projects` | Host folder with your repositories (default `./projects`) |
| `CODX_JUNIOR_WEB_PORT` | no | `8080` | Web UI port (default `19981`) |

You can pass them on the command line (`./up.sh --provider … --key …`), or write
them in `.env` (copy `.env.example`), or export them in your shell.

### Provider presets

`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_PROVIDER` selects a preset; codx-junior fills in the base URL,
the chat model, the wiki model and the embeddings model for you.

| Provider | Base URL used | Default chat model | Embeddings model | Get a key |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `openai` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | `gpt-4.1-mini` (`gpt-4.1` for wiki) | `text-embedding-3-small` (1536) | platform.openai.com/api-keys |
| `deepseek` | `https://api.deepseek.com/v1` | `deepseek-chat` | *none* → RAG disabled | platform.deepseek.com/api_keys |
| `gemini` | `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai` | `gemini-2.0-flash` | `text-embedding-004` (768) | aistudio.google.com/app/apikey |
| `openrouter` | `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` | `openai/gpt-4o-mini` | *none* → RAG disabled | openrouter.ai/keys |
| `mistral` | `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` | `mistral-large-latest` | `mistral-embed` (1024) | console.mistral.ai/api-keys |
| `groq` | `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` | `llama-3.3-70b-versatile` | *none* → RAG disabled | console.groq.com/keys |
| `ollama` | `http://localhost:11434/v1` | `llama3.1` | `nomic-embed-text` (768) | local, no key |
| `custom` | `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` | `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_MODEL` | `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_EMBEDDINGS_MODEL` | — |

Notes:

* **Everything goes through the `openai` client.** Any gateway exposing
  `/chat/completions` + `/embeddings` with a `/v1` path works as `custom`
  (LiteLLM, Portkey, vLLM, Ollama, LM Studio, Azure OpenAI proxy…).
* **Anthropic** has no OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Run LiteLLM in front of it
  and use `--provider custom --url http://litellm:4000/v1`.
* Providers without an embeddings endpoint keep **knowledge/RAG search disabled**
  (the rest of the app works). Add an embeddings model later from *Global
  settings → AI models*.

---

## 2. What codx-junior configures by itself

On the first start the API reads the settings above and, **only if no provider
has been configured yet**, it:

1. creates the `AIProvider` (name = the provider you chose) with its base URL
   and key;
2. creates the models `knowledge` (chat/coding/RAG/guardrail) and `embeddings`
   (plus a `wiki` entry when the preset uses a different model for the wiki);
3. points the five global model slots (`llm_model`, `rag_model`, `wiki_model`,
   `guardrail_model`, `embeddings_model`) at them;
4. writes a summary to `$CODX_JUNIOR_CONFIG_FOLDER/bootstrap.json`.

Result: you open the UI, pick a project, and the chat works. No settings page,
no model import, no "no model configured" dead end.

It is **idempotent and non-destructive**: an installation already configured
from the UI is never touched. To re-apply (e.g. after rotating a key):

```bash
docker exec codx-junior curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap/apply
docker exec codx-junior curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:19980/api/bootstrap   # inspect
```

`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_FORCE=1` makes every start re-apply it;
`CODX_JUNIOR_AI_BOOTSTRAP=0` disables it entirely.

The key itself is **not** written to the settings files: the provider stores
`$CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` and it is expanded from the environment at use time
(`global_settings.get_provider_settings`).

---

## 3. What this deployment leaves out

| Component of the full stack | Why it is not here | How to get it back |
|---|---|---|
| **client** container (Node + `vite preview`) | the SPA is compiled in a builder stage and served by nginx | never needed |
| **api-background** container | runs as a supervisord program in the same container | never needed |
| **traefik** | same-origin: nginx proxies `/api` to the API | add a proxy in front, or use the server tier |
| **localai** | replaced by "bring your own provider key" | `codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml` |
| **milvus** | not needed: the vector store is embedded LanceDB, running in the API process | never needed (point at your own Milvus only if you have data in it) |
| **analytics-init / codx-junior-init** | their `mkdir`/`chown` work is done by the entrypoint | — |
| torch / sentence-transformers / vLLM / Playwright / TeX / Tesseract / Firefox | runtime deps of optional features; now `pip` extras (`.[local-models,browser]`) | full deployment installs them |

Features **not available** in the demo without extra work: local (offline)
embeddings, document → PDF/DOCX conversion, Tesseract OCR, browser/computer
sessions and workspaces (they need `/var/run/docker.sock`).

### Knowledge / RAG: built in, no vector database to run

Knowledge is a **built-in** feature of this deployment: the vector store is
**LanceDB**, embedded on disk and running in the API process. There is no Milvus
container, no `--knowledge` flag and no extra RAM.

- **One switch**: `CODX_JUNIOR_KNOWLEDGE_BACKEND` — `lancedb` (default,
  embedded), `milvus` (your external server, needs
  `pip install 'codx-junior[milvus]'`) or `none`.
- **Native hybrid search**: BM25 full-text + dense vectors fused with RRF — the
  same result shape as the Milvus backend, so the UI is identical.
- **RAG also needs an embeddings model.** `deepseek`, `openrouter` and `groq` do
  not provide one, so on those keys search stays **lexical** (full-text) instead
  of failing; `openai`, `gemini`, `mistral` and `ollama` configure one
  automatically.
- **It degrades, never breaks.** If the embeddings stack cannot load, the dense
  leg is switched off with a single log warning and the lexical leg keeps
  answering; knowledge never stops the API from booting.

So there is nothing to enable: the chat, the projects, the agent, the file tools
and knowledge search all work with one container.
To enable the docker-dependent features, uncomment the socket mount in
`docker-compose.yaml`. Be aware that it gives the container control of the host
Docker daemon.

---

## 4. Operating it

```bash
./up.sh                      # start (idempotent)
./up.sh --build              # build the image from source instead of pulling
docker compose logs -f codx-junior
docker compose down          # stop (volumes are kept)
docker compose down -v       # stop and delete settings/analytics
```

Ports and volumes:

| | |
|---|---|
| `19981` | Web UI (published) |
| `19980` | API (internal, proxied by nginx) |
| volume `codx-junior-settings` | global settings, per-project `.codx`, presets |
| volume `codx-junior-analytics` | token usage, AI logs, API metrics |
| bind `${CODX_JUNIOR_PROJECTS_PATH}` | your repositories |

The health check is `GET /api/health`. `docker compose ps` shows `healthy` when
the API answers.

---

## 5. Development deployment (unchanged)

The watch/reload deployment is `codx-junior/docker-compose.yaml` (+ the
`docker-compose.build.yaml` overlay when the images still have to be built). There
is **no `docker-compose.dev.yaml`**: the source mount and `DEBUG=1` are hardcoded in
that compose file, `scripts/run_api.sh` syncs the environment on start, and the web
client only runs the Vite dev server when you switch its service to `DEBUG=1`
(it ships with `DEBUG=0`, i.e. `npm run preview`). Use it when you hack on
codx-junior itself, not to show it to a user.

Two knobs make the source deployment behave like this one:

* `CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL=1` — skip the recursive `chown` and `uv sync` that
  `scripts/run_api.sh` runs on every start.
* `CODX_JUNIOR_API_EXTRAS` — extras installed by `scripts/install_api.sh`
  (default `local-models,browser`, empty for a slim install).

---

## 6. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| UI loads, chat answers "no model configured" | the bootstrap did not run: check `docker exec codx-junior curl -s localhost:19980/api/bootstrap` and that `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_KEY` is set in `.env`. |
| `401` / `invalid api key` in the logs | wrong key, or `CODX_JUNIOR_AI_API_URL` missing `/v1`. |
| Chat works, "knowledge search" finds nothing | check the embeddings model for the preset (see §3): `deepseek`, `openrouter` and `groq` have none, so search stays lexical |
| Container is `unhealthy` | `docker compose logs --tail 100 codx-junior`; the API log is `api.log` inside `$CODX_SUPERVISOR_LOG_FOLDER`. |
| Port 19981 already in use | `./up.sh --port 8080`. |
| Projects folder empty / permission denied | `./up.sh --projects /absolute/path`; the demo container runs as root so it can write to host folders. |

Deeper analysis of the original deployment and the full change list:
[`../FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md`](../FAST-DEPLOYMENT.md).

```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Compatibility shim — do not add logic here.
#
# The Docker Hub tools (dockerhub_publish / dockerhub_whoami) execute their
# helper script with the API working directory as cwd, so the configured

set -euo pipefail
root="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
cd "$root"
exec ./scripts/dockerhub_publish.sh "$@"

#!/bin/bash
# Dynamically set CODX_JUNIOR_PATH to the parent directory of the script
export CODX_JUNIOR_PATH="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
echo "CODX_JUNIOR_PATH: $CODX_JUNIOR_PATH"
echo "Starting api USER: ${USER} ($(id -u):$(id -g)) HOME: ${HOME}"

# A packaged image (see codx-junior-installer/demo) already ships the venv and a
# source tree it must not touch: the recursive chown and `uv sync` below are
# installation steps, not start-up steps, and cost tens of seconds per restart.
# Set CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL=1 to skip them.
if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL" != "1" ]; then
  echo "Fix permissions"
  sudo chown -R ${USER} ${HOME}
  sudo chown ${USER} /var/run/docker.sock 2>/dev/null || true
fi

source ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/set_env.sh

export PYTHONPATH=${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/api

cd ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/api


# Run the FastAPI application using uvicorn
echo "Checking venv: '${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}' ..."
if [ ! -d "${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}/bin" ]; then
  echo "!!! venv not found. Installing at: ${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}"
  bash ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/scripts/install_api.sh
else
  echo "venv found!"
fi

source ${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}/bin/activate

if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL" != "1" ]; then
  # Sync the environment with pyproject.toml / uv.lock on start (development and
  # source-mounted deployments only: it downloads packages).
  uv sync
fi

echo "codx-junior api BACKGROUND: '${CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND}' DEBUG: '${DEBUG}'"

API_PORT=$CODX_JUNIOR_API_PORT
if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND" != "" ]; then
  API_PORT=$CODX_JUNIOR_API_PORT_BACKGROUND
fi

if [ "$DEBUG" == "" ]; then
  echo "Running PROD api"
  # ONE worker by default: Socket.IO keeps the connected sessions (and the
  # in-memory CancellationTokens of the running turns) inside the process, so
  # with several workers a client reconnects/re-emits against another worker and
  # its chat looks stuck. Scale explicitly with WEB_CONCURRENCY only when a
  # shared Socket.IO message queue is configured.
  uvicorn codx.junior.main:app --workers ${WEB_CONCURRENCY:-1} --host 0.0.0.0 --port $API_PORT
elif [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD" == "1" ] || [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD" == "true" ]; then
  # Opt-in source reload for development ONLY. Never enable it when the AI
  # agents edit the project itself: every file change restarts uvicorn and
  # interrupts the in-flight chat turns (the harness would kill its own work).
  echo "Running DEBUG api with source reload"
  uvicorn codx.junior.main:app --reload --reload-exclude ".venv" --host 0.0.0.0 --port $API_PORT
else
  # DEBUG=1 only raises logging/verbosity here: the API is supervised by
  # supervisor/Docker and must not restart itself while a turn is running.
  echo "Running DEBUG api (no source reload; set CODX_JUNIOR_API_RELOAD=1 to enable)"
  uvicorn codx.junior.main:app --workers ${WEB_CONCURRENCY:-1} --host 0.0.0.0 --port $API_PORT
fi

"""
Docker Hub management tools.

Registry-side companion of ``docker_tools``: the docker tools build and run
images locally, these ones publish them to Docker Hub and drive the repository
catalogue (tags, digests, deletions) through the Docker Hub API v2.

Configuration is environment driven, exactly like ``scripts/dockerhub_publish.sh``:

    DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE   organisation/user (default: codxjuniorai)
    DOCKERHUB_USER        registry user (default: the namespace)
    DOCKERHUB_TOKEN       access token; required for anything that writes
    DOCKERHUB_REGISTRY    registry host (default: docker.io)

Read-only calls work anonymously for public repositories; pushing and deleting
always require the token, which is never echoed in a response.

Made with <3 by codx-junior
"""

import base64
import json
import logging
import os
import re
import shlex
import subprocess
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

from .model import ToolResponse

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

DEFAULT_NAMESPACE = "codxjuniorai"
HUB_API = "https://hub.docker.com/v2"
PUBLISH_SCRIPT = "scripts/dockerhub_publish.sh"
_TIMEOUT = 30


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Configuration helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _namespace(namespace: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
    return (namespace or os.environ.get("DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE") or DEFAULT_NAMESPACE).strip()


def _user() -> str:
    return (os.environ.get("DOCKERHUB_USER") or _namespace()).strip()


_ACTIVE_SETTINGS = None
_TOKEN_CACHE: Dict[str, str] = {}


def _bind(settings) -> None:
    """Remember the settings of the running tool so _token() can reach the vault."""
    global _ACTIVE_SETTINGS
    if settings is not None and settings is not _ACTIVE_SETTINGS:
        _ACTIVE_SETTINGS = settings
        _TOKEN_CACHE.clear()


def _vault_token(settings=None) -> str:
    """Read DOCKERHUB_TOKEN from the project secret vault (value never logged)."""
    try:
        from codx.junior.security.ciso.policy import resolve_policy
        from codx.junior.security.ciso.vault import SecretVault

        target = settings or _ACTIVE_SETTINGS
        vault = SecretVault(_project_dir(target), resolve_policy(target))
        value, _error = vault.get_value("vault", "DOCKERHUB_TOKEN")
        return (value or "").strip()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - the vault is optional for this tool
        logger.debug("DOCKERHUB_TOKEN not resolvable from the vault", exc_info=True)
        return ""


def _token() -> str:
    """Token from the environment, falling back to the project secret vault."""
    value = os.environ.get("DOCKERHUB_TOKEN", "").strip()
    if value:
        return value
    if "vault" not in _TOKEN_CACHE:
        _TOKEN_CACHE["vault"] = _vault_token()
    return _TOKEN_CACHE["vault"]


def _auth_header() -> Optional[str]:
    """Basic auth header for the Docker Hub API, or None when anonymous."""
    token = _token()
    if not token:
        return None
    raw = f"{_user()}:{token}".encode("utf-8")
    return "Basic " + base64.b64encode(raw).decode("ascii")


def _validate(value: str, field: str, pattern: str = r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-\.]+$") -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
        raise ValueError(f"{field} is required")
    value = value.strip()
    if not re.match(pattern, value):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid {field}: {value!r}")
    return value


def _api(
    path: str,
    method: str = "GET",
    body: Optional[Dict] = None,
    query: Optional[Dict] = None,
) -> Dict:
    """Call the Docker Hub API and return the decoded JSON payload."""
    url = f"{HUB_API}/{path.lstrip('/')}"
    if query:
        url = f"{url}?{urllib.parse.urlencode(query)}"

    data = None
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json"}
    if body is not None:
        data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    authorization = _auth_header()
    if authorization:
        headers["Authorization"] = authorization

    request = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, headers=headers, method=method)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=_TIMEOUT) as response:
            payload = response.read().decode("utf-8")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        detail = exc.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")[:500]
        raise RuntimeError(f"Docker Hub API {method} {path} -> HTTP {exc.code}: {detail}")
    except urllib.error.URLError as exc:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Docker Hub API unreachable: {exc.reason}")

    if not payload:
        return {}
    try:
        return json.loads(payload)
    except json.JSONDecodeError:
        return {"raw": payload}


def _project_dir(settings) -> str:
    """Return the project root that actually holds PUBLISH_SCRIPT.

    ``codx_path`` points at the control plane (``<project>/.codx``) and the API
    process runs with ``<project>/api`` as cwd, so neither is the repo root the
    publish script lives in: every candidate is checked against the script, and
    the repo root is derived from this file as a last resort.
    """
    candidates: List[str] = []
    for attribute in ("project_path", "project_dir", "codx_path"):
        value = getattr(settings, attribute, None)
        if not value:
            continue
        path = os.path.abspath(str(value))
        candidates += [path, os.path.dirname(path)]
    here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    candidates.append(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(here)))))
    candidates.append(os.getcwd())

    for path in candidates:
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(path, PUBLISH_SCRIPT)):
            return path
    for path in candidates:
        if os.path.isdir(path):
            return path
    return os.getcwd()

def dockerhub_whoami(namespace: Optional[str] = None, **kwargs) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Report how the Docker Hub integration is configured and whether the token works.

    Checks the namespace, the login user, whether a token is present (it is
    never printed) and whether the token is accepted by the registry API.

    Args:
        namespace: Docker Hub namespace to inspect (default: ``DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE``).
        **kwargs: settings / user injected by the engine.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: configuration summary plus the token status.
    """
    try:
        target = _namespace(namespace)
        has_token = bool(_token())
        lines = [
            f"namespace: {target}",
            f"user: {_user()}",
            f"token: {'present' if has_token else 'missing'}",
            f"hub: https://hub.docker.com/u/{target}",
        ]
        status = "anonymous"
        if has_token:
            try:
                _api("user/")
                status = "token accepted"
            except RuntimeError as exc:
                status = f"token rejected ({exc})"
        lines.append(f"auth: {status}")
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response="Docker Hub configuration\n" + "\n".join(f"- {line}" for line in lines),
            llm_response="Docker Hub configuration:\n" + "\n".join(lines),
        )
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - tool boundary
        logger.exception("dockerhub_whoami failed")
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"Docker Hub check failed: {exc}",
            llm_response=f"dockerhub_whoami error: {exc}",
        )


def dockerhub_publish(
    tags: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    image_name: Optional[str] = None,
    namespace: Optional[str] = None,
    platforms: Optional[str] = None,
    dockerfile: Optional[str] = None,
    context: Optional[str] = None,
    build_args: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
    push: bool = True,
    no_cache: bool = False,
    dry_run: bool = False,
    timeout: int = 1800,
    **kwargs,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Build the project image and publish it to Docker Hub.

    Runs ``scripts/dockerhub_publish.sh`` with the environment variables it
    expects, so the AI path and the CI path publish exactly the same way.

    Args:
        tags: Tags to push for the same build (e.g. ``["1.4.0", "latest"]``).
        image_name: Repository name (default: ``IMAGE_NAME`` or ``codx-junior``).
        namespace: Docker Hub organisation (default: ``DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE``).
        platforms: buildx platforms (default: ``linux/amd64,linux/arm64``).
        dockerfile: Dockerfile path relative to the project.
        context: Build context relative to the project.
        build_args: ``--build-arg`` pairs.
        push: Push to the registry (requires ``DOCKERHUB_TOKEN``).
        no_cache: Disable the build cache.
        dry_run: Only print the docker commands.
        timeout: Seconds before the build is killed (60-3600).
        **kwargs: settings / user injected by the engine.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: the command, its output tail and the published references.
    """
    settings = kwargs.get("settings")
    _bind(settings)
    try:
        if not isinstance(timeout, int) or timeout < 60 or timeout > 3600:
            raise ValueError("timeout must be an integer between 60-3600 seconds")

        project_dir = _project_dir(settings)
        script = os.path.join(project_dir, PUBLISH_SCRIPT)
        if not os.path.isfile(script):
            raise ValueError(f"publish script not found: {PUBLISH_SCRIPT}")

        target_namespace = _validate(_namespace(namespace), "namespace")
        repository = _validate(
            image_name or os.environ.get("IMAGE_NAME") or "codx-junior", "image_name"
        )
        tag_list = [str(tag).strip() for tag in (tags or []) if str(tag).strip()]
        if not tag_list:
            tag_list = [os.environ.get("IMAGE_TAG", "latest")]

        if push and not _token():
            raise ValueError("DOCKERHUB_TOKEN is required to push (or set push=False)")

        env = dict(os.environ)
        env.update(
            {
                "DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE": target_namespace,
                "DOCKERHUB_USER": _user(),
                "IMAGE_NAME": repository,
                "IMAGE_TAGS": ",".join(tag_list),
                "PUSH": "true" if push else "false",
                "NO_CACHE": "true" if no_cache else "false",
                "DRY_RUN": "true" if dry_run else "false",
            }
        )
        if platforms:
            env["PLATFORMS"] = str(platforms)
        if dockerfile:
            env["DOCKERFILE"] = str(dockerfile)
        if context:
            env["CONTEXT"] = str(context)
        if build_args:
            env["BUILD_ARGS"] = " ".join(
                f"{key}={value}" for key, value in build_args.items()
            )

        command = ["bash", script]
        logger.info("Publishing %s/%s tags=%s", target_namespace, repository, tag_list)
        completed = subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 - fixed script, no shell
            command,
            cwd=project_dir,
            env=env,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=timeout,
        )

        refs = [f"{target_namespace}/{repository}:{tag}" for tag in tag_list]
        tail = ((completed.stdout or "") + "\n" + (completed.stderr or "")).strip()[-4000:]
        if completed.returncode != 0:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=(
                    f"Publish failed for {', '.join(refs)} "
                    f"(exit {completed.returncode})\n\n```\n{tail}\n```"
                ),
                llm_response=(
                    f"`{' '.join(shlex.quote(part) for part in command)}` exited "
                    f"{completed.returncode}.\nOutput:\n{tail}"
                ),
            )

        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=(
                f"Published {', '.join(refs)}\n\n"
                f"https://hub.docker.com/r/{target_namespace}/{repository}/tags\n\n"
                f"```\n{tail[-1500:]}\n```"
            ),
            llm_response=f"Published: {', '.join(refs)}\nOutput tail:\n{tail}",
        )
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - tool boundary
        logger.exception("dockerhub_publish failed")
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"Publish failed: {exc}",
            llm_response=f"dockerhub_publish error: {exc}",
        )


def dockerhub_tags(
    repository: str,
    namespace: Optional[str] = None,
    page_size: int = 25,
    name_filter: Optional[str] = None,
    **kwargs,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    List the tags published for one repository, with digests and last update.

    Args:
        repository: Repository name (e.g. ``codx-junior``).
        namespace: Docker Hub organisation (default: ``DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE``).
        page_size: Tags per page (1-100).
        name_filter: Only keep tags whose name contains this text.
        **kwargs: settings / user injected by the engine.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: table of tags with last pushed date and digest prefix.
    """
    try:
        target = _validate(_namespace(namespace), "namespace")
        repo = _validate(repository, "repository")
        page_size = max(1, min(int(page_size), 100))

        payload = _api(
            f"repositories/{target}/{repo}/tags",
            query={"page_size": page_size, "ordering": "last_updated"},
        )
        results = payload.get("results") or []
        if name_filter:
            needle = name_filter.lower()
            results = [tag for tag in results if needle in str(tag.get("name", "")).lower()]

        if not results:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"No tags found for {target}/{repo}.",
                llm_response=f"No tags for {target}/{repo} (filter={name_filter!r}).",
            )

        rows = []
        for tag in results:
            digest = str(tag.get("digest") or "")
            rows.append(
                {
                    "name": tag.get("name"),
                    "digest": digest[:19],
                    "size_mb": round((tag.get("full_size") or 0) / (1024 * 1024), 1),
                    "updated": str(tag.get("last_updated") or "")[:19],
                    "architectures": ",".join(
                        sorted(
                            {
                                image.get("architecture", "")
                                for image in (tag.get("images") or [])
                                if image.get("architecture")
                            }
                        )
                    ),
                }
            )

        table = "\n".join(
            f"| {row['name']} | {row['updated']} | {row['size_mb']} MB | "
            f"{row['architectures'] or '-'} | `{row['digest']}` |"
            for row in rows
        )
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=(
                f"Tags for {target}/{repo}\n\n"
                "| tag | updated | size | arch | digest |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n" + table
            ),
            llm_response=(
                f"Tags for {target}/{repo}: "
                + json.dumps([row["name"] for row in rows])
                + f"\n\n{table}"
            ),
        )
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - tool boundary
        logger.exception("dockerhub_tags failed")
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"Could not list tags: {exc}",
            llm_response=f"dockerhub_tags error: {exc}",
        )


def dockerhub_repositories(
    namespace: Optional[str] = None,
    page_size: int = 25,
    **kwargs,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    List the repositories of the Docker Hub organisation.

    Args:
        namespace: Docker Hub organisation (default: ``DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE``).
        page_size: Repositories per page (1-100).
        **kwargs: settings / user injected by the engine.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: repositories with pull count, last updated and visibility.
    """
    try:
        target = _validate(_namespace(namespace) if namespace else _user(), "namespace")
        page_size = max(1, min(int(page_size), 100))

        payload = _api(
            f"repositories/{target}/",
            query={"page_size": page_size, "ordering": "last_updated"},
        )
        results = payload.get("results") or []
        if not results:
            return ToolResponse(
                user_response=f"No repositories visible for {target}.",
                llm_response=f"No repositories for {target}.",
            )

        rows = []
        for repo in results:
            rows.append(
                {
                    "name": repo.get("name"),
                    "private": bool(repo.get("is_private")),
                    "pulls": repo.get("pull_count", 0),
                    "updated": str(repo.get("last_updated") or "")[:19],
                }
            )
        table = "\n".join(
            f"| {row['name']} | {'private' if row['private'] else 'public'} | "
            f"{row['pulls']} | {row['updated']} |"
            for row in rows
        )
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=(
                f"Repositories in {target}\n\n"
                "| repository | visibility | pulls | updated |\n|---|---|---|---|\n" + table
            ),
            llm_response=f"Repositories in {target}:\n{table}",
        )
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - tool boundary
        logger.exception("dockerhub_repositories failed")
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"Could not list repositories: {exc}",
            llm_response=f"dockerhub_repositories error: {exc}",
        )


def dockerhub_delete_tag(
    repository: str,
    tag: str,
    namespace: Optional[str] = None,
    confirm: bool = False,
    **kwargs,
) -> ToolResponse:
    """
    Delete one published tag from Docker Hub (destructive, requires confirm).

    Args:
        repository: Repository name (e.g. ``codx-junior``).
        tag: Tag to delete (``latest`` is refused: retag first).
        namespace: Docker Hub organisation (default: ``DOCKERHUB_NAMESPACE``).
        confirm: Must be True, otherwise nothing is deleted.
        **kwargs: settings / user injected by the engine.

    Returns:
        ToolResponse: the deletion outcome.
    """
    try:
        if not confirm:
            raise ValueError("confirm=True is required to delete a published tag")
        if not _token():
            raise ValueError("DOCKERHUB_TOKEN is required to delete a tag")
        if str(tag).strip().lower() in ("latest", "stable"):
            raise ValueError(f"refusing to delete the floating tag {tag!r}")

        target = _validate(_namespace(namespace), "namespace")
        repo = _validate(repository, "repository")
        clean_tag = _validate(tag, "tag", r"^[a-zA-Z0-9_\-.]+$")

        _api(f"repositories/{target}/{repo}/tags/{clean_tag}/", method="DELETE")
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"Deleted {target}/{repo}:{clean_tag} from Docker Hub.",
            llm_response=f"Deleted tag {clean_tag} of {target}/{repo}.",
        )
    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - tool boundary
        logger.exception("dockerhub_delete_tag failed")
        return ToolResponse(
            user_response=f"Could not delete tag: {exc}",
            llm_response=f"dockerhub_delete_tag error: {exc}",
        )

"""Publish the release image through the Docker Hub tool in a FRESH process.

The api server imports its modules once at boot, so a patch to
``codx.junior.tools.dockerhub_tools`` only takes effect after a restart -- and a
restart kills the process serving the chat. This entrypoint imports the current
working tree, so the vault fallback of ``_token()`` is active immediately.

Usage (inside codx-junior-api):
    python3 tmp/_publish_vault.py [repository] [tag ...]
"""

import os
import subprocess
import sys

REPO_ROOT = os.environ.get("CODX_JUNIOR_PATH", "/home/codx-junior/codx-junior")
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, "api"))

DOCKERFILE = "codx-junior-installer/demo/Dockerfile"


def _git(*args: str) -> str:
    """Best-effort git query used for the image provenance labels."""
    try:
        return subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", REPO_ROOT, *args],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,
            check=False,
        ).stdout.strip()
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - provenance is cosmetic
        return ""


def main() -> int:
